sense.text:
“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” We should not be loving this world and the things of this world. “If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” If any brother or sister has that spirit, loving this place, the love of God is not in you.

The state of mind to have is: I want to be up out of here, I hate this place. That is how we are supposed to be molding ourselves. The things you see in the world, you are not supposed to be following. You are supposed to be separate.

“The lust of the flesh” is what this flesh desires. “The lust of the eyes” is the things you see, and today that is what everybody is on: TikTok, social media. That is where the minds of a lot of young brothers and sisters are. “The pride of life” is: look what I accomplished, I got this car, this house, three houses over here. All of it “is not of the Father, but is of the world.”

A TikTok challenge everybody is doing, the dance to the song Feeling On My Body, is of the world. The song is all about sex, and the dance acts like they are eating something. Young brothers and sisters, even in IUIC, watch stuff like that and mimic it, and some school sisters were doing that dumb stupid dance on the new moon. Young sisters and grown sisters are not supposed to be doing that. That is the lust of the eyes: seeing it on social media and thinking it is cool.
“And the world passeth away”: all these things are going to disappear soon. They are going to pass away.

precepts.why:
In that song she says she loves an eater. Does that mean eating food? “Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.” She is not talking about eating food. She is talking about eating sausage.

That is the characteristic of an adulterous, wicked woman: she does it, wipes her mouth, and says she has done nothing wrong. Some sisters do not know that and get caught up in it, but the dance is about sucking rod. That is what it is about.

So sisters should not be doing those dumb stupid dances. They do not even understand what is behind it. That is the lust of the eyes. They think they are eating food, but they are conjuring demons, eating rod. It is not innocent.

sense.text: “The things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.” What is heard is committed to faithful men, so that they may be able to teach others also.

“Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” We have to endure hardness like soldiers. We are soldiers of Jesus Christ, and that is the state of mind every last one of us should have: the state of mind of a soldier, the state of mind that we are at war.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”: if you are warring, you are not supposed to love this world or be caught up with the affairs of this life. The things in this world are set up to take us out. That is what you are warring against, so you cannot get caught up in it.

“That he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Christ chose us to be soldiers. We are in Christ’s army, and there is a war going on. A lot of brothers and sisters do not fully understand that. They think this is just Bible study, just a regular church group, not understanding they are soldiers in Christ’s army and at war.

So you have to know who you are at war with, what you are fighting against, and when the war started. When you come to the truth, things get crazy. Some get taken out by snipers; Satan takes some out, and that is why some brothers and sisters are not seen any more. Some are wounded right now, hand cut off, foot cut off, crawling, and Satan is about to end you. Yet a lot will not go to the brothers and say, Satan is whooping my ass, I am losing the fight.
“For God created man to be immortal”: Adam was created to be immortal. “And made him to be an image of his own eternity”: he was made just like the Father.

“Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” That is how Adam died: Satan envied him. This shows who we are fighting and when the war began. It began in Genesis, and Genesis means beginning: the war between good and evil, between the sons of God and the sons of the devil.

What started that war is when Satan attacked Adam, and he attacked Adam through his wife. And when Adam fell, all his sons that were in paradise with him fell.

precepts.why:
Satan did not just attack Adam. He attacked Adam’s kingdom, including all of us. “Even so also is Israel’s portion. Because for their sakes I made the world”: the world was made for the sake of Israel, the 12 tribes of Israel, the so-called blacks and Hispanics.

“And when Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” That is when Satan made his move on Adam and tricked Adam’s wife. “Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail”: we have to catch hell. That travail is also going to war, us warring against Satan and his children. The entrances became “few and evil, full of perils”, and “very painful.” When did this happen? When Adam sinned.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world is Adam’s kingdom. The move Satan made against Adam was not against Adam alone but his kingdom: we all fell when Adam fell. All 12 tribes were in paradise, and that immortal fruit means we were living forever. Nobody had a trace of thought of the elder world; only now is the Lord showing us little bits and pieces of what was taking place back then.

“If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.” God wants us to labour to enter back into those things. The labour is our coming on this earth, keeping the commandments and doing what is commanded us, enduring trials and tribulation, to enter back into that place.

So the war started through envy of the devil, when he made a move on Adam’s kingdom by deceiving his wife.

sense.text:
“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field”: the serpent is Satan, the devil. “Which the Lord God had made”: God created him to be exactly who he was. He was subtil, he was tricky.

It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake. It is talking about Satan. He is called a serpent because he has a forked tongue, because he is slick.

precepts.why: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He made him what he is, the subtil one of Genesis 3.

sense.text:
The verses before it tell how Satan tricked Eve. Satan made a move on Adam through his wife, the weaker vessel. He caused Eve to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Now the Most High God comes and deals with Adam, Eve and Satan, and judgment comes on all three.

“Because thou hast done this”: because of what Satan did; the serpent is Satan. “Thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field” is not talking about cattle and beasts. Remember where this is: in paradise. He is cursed above all the creations God created that were up there in the heavens.

“Upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.” This is an analogy, Satan’s judgment. Man was created from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being; he is going to be on the earth eating dust. “All the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: for what he did, Satan will be destroyed by the Lord in the future.

There is a lot said in that one verse. Eating dust is also the Lord giving Satan power over the earth. Satan became the tempter. That is his judgment, and soon he will be destroyed.

“And I will put enmity between thee and the woman.” This shows when the war began. Satan made a move on Adam through his wife, so the woman will hate him.

“And between thy seed and her seed.” Her seed today is the 12 tribes of Israel. His seed today is the so-called Caucasians, the Edomites. Back when the Lord said this, Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants, and her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage. The prophecy is that there will always be a war between us and Satan’s seed. That is when the war began.

So when the Bible says be soldiers of Jesus Christ, who are you fighting? Ask Christians and they say the spiritual demon, Satan. Yes, we are fighting Satan: those wicked thoughts, Satan whispering in your ears. But we are also fighting his children, his physical counterpart. When you read about Satan and the devil, it is not only that spiritual demon. It is interchangeable: it is talking about him and his children.

“It shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Their seed, the Romans, crucified Christ; and the Lord is going to take down Satan and his children. That is the judgment: for what you did, the Lord is going to destroy you and your children.

precepts.why:
“Dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life” is the Lord giving Satan power over the earth. The devil took Christ “up into an high mountain” and “shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me.”

When was the power of this earth delivered unto Satan? In Genesis 3. That is when the power to rule this earth was given to him.

“And to whomsoever I will I give it.” He gave that power first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white men in these last days. That is why he is able to create all this technology. Satan has power on this earth, and it was given to him in Genesis 3.

This also happened after Satan was judged. “The sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. Satan goes before the Lord.

“Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking is the dust he is going to eat. Satan’s job is to walk around this earth to see who he can tempt and destroy. He became the tempter; that is his judgment, and soon he will be destroyed.

Here Satan’s children are born into the earth. Eve bare Cain and his brother Abel. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” The Lord had respect unto Abel and his offering, but unto Cain and his offering he had not respect, and Cain was very wroth.

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” If you do good you will be accepted; if you do evil, Satan is going to rule over you. Cain became the children of Satan; Cain served Satan.

“Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” This is the fulfilment of Genesis 3:15: I will put enmity between thy seed and her seed. The enmity starts here. Cain became the seed of Satan and killed his brother, our forefather Abel. That was the first blood shed in the war, the first murder on the earth.

This shows Cain was the seed of Satan. “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was of the devil; he and his descendants were the children of the devil, the seed of the devil. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil.

In the beginning Cain became the children of Satan, and the destruction of that world came because of Cain and his descendants. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then. He corrupted everyone on the earth, including the sons of God. So God destroyed everybody on the earth, and now the sons of God and the sons of the devil are coming back.

They came back right here. Rebekah conceived, “and the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus?” If I am blessed, why is this happening? “And the Lord said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb.” Those two nations are the so-called Negroes and Hispanics, the 12 tribes of Israel, Jacob; and “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”: the other manner of people is Esau, the so-called white man.

People think the fight between Jacob and Esau, between blacks and whites, started in slavery, in the Jim Crow era, in the civil rights era. No. It started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and it is reborn here as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. We represent good; the white man represents evil. Cain represents evil; Abel and Seth represent good. Do not get it wrong: a lot of our people followed after Cain back then, which is what Jude is about, and today a lot of our people follow after Esau, and they have become the children of the devil themselves.

“The one people shall be stronger than the other people”: that is Jacob, the 12 tribes of Israel. “And the elder shall serve the younger”: that is future tense.

“The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment.” Esau was born with no pigment in his skin, so you could see the blood under his skin: he is red. The same with Cain in the beginning: the earth cursed Cain, and he lost all his pigment.

“His hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That goes back to Genesis 3:15: thou shalt bruise his heel. This birth is prophetic. Jacob holding on to Esau’s heel represents our King, our Lord, coming to destroy Esau and the wicked, Satan and his children.

“Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth”: Esau will dwell in the best place on the earth, wherever he wants. That is his blessing. “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” Living by the sword means by war. All the wars taking place on the earth for the last hundreds of years: who starts them? Esau.

So the enmity came back. Cain came back as Esau: the seed of the devil, his children, came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob.

sense.text:
When the Bible talks about the devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the children and their father. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them.

“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison.” Did the literal devil, a spiritual demon, snatch somebody and throw them in prison? No. The devil here is his children.

precepts.why:
“Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.”

Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He put Peter in prison and killed James. So when the Bible says the devil shall cast you into prison, at that time it is talking about Herod, about Satan’s children, about Rome. When it says devil it is interchangeable: it is his children. Satan uses his children to do what he wants done.

sense.text: Job was “perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.” He hated evil and loved God.

He had seven sons and three daughters, seven thousand sheep, “three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household.” Job was rich: “the greatest of all the men of the east.”

His sons “feasted in their houses, every one his day.” Everyone his day: that could be going into what is celebrated today, birthdays.

When the days of their feasting were gone about, “Job sent and sanctified them”: he cleansed them, and offered burnt offerings. Why? “For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts.” Something in that celebration was not right, so Job sanctified them and asked God for mercy for them. “Thus did Job continually.”

This is in the heavens. “Satan came also among them.” Satan has access to the heaven, and he is also “walking up and down” on this earth. What is he doing there? Destroying souls, destroying the sons of God, warring with the sons of God on the earth.

Satan comes from a Hebrew word meaning adversary, accuser, opponent. He is our adversary and our King’s adversary. Not only that spiritual demon: his seed, his children, are also our adversary, as Genesis 3:15 says. The white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. Devil means deceiver: the same way Satan deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why the so-called white man is called the devil, and called Satan because he is our adversary and God’s adversary.

“Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth”: the Most High bragging about his servant. Job is righteous; he hates evil.

Everything Job went through is a template for what every last one of us is going to go through in this truth, on different levels. Satan is going to come at every last one of us. Job is a lesson for all of us.

“Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him”: the hedge is angels. Job had angels protecting him, so Satan could not get to him. Satan wanted Job bad, but the Lord was protecting him. The hedge was “about his house” too, his kids and his wife, and “about all that he hath on every side”: blessings, and angels protecting all of it.

“But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” Satan said, take away all those things and he will turn his back on you. But for that to happen, the hedge has to be taken away first.

“Behold, all that he hath is in thy power.” God removed the angels, the hedge that was protecting Job. That is what we will go through, every last one of us: your name is going to come before the Lord when Satan comes for you. “Only upon himself put not forth thine hand”: do not touch Job, but touch everything else he has.

“So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.” Satan listened to God. That dumb stupid doctrine Christians teach, that Satan rebelled against God and there was war in heaven, is not it.

“The Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword.” The Sabeans are the Ethiopians. But wasn’t it Satan doing it? Yes, and people literally did it. When Satan attacks, he uses people: that boss on your job, that chick on your job, that dude on your job. Satan is in that person, using that person.

Brothers, the chick on your job who keeps walking by giving you the eye: that is Satan right there. We have to be able to see Satan when he is making his moves.

“While he was yet speaking”: everything happened at the same time. Sometimes when Satan attacks he hits you from all sides. It is not just one thing; everything goes wrong in your life. When that happens, understand it is Satan. The fire fell from heaven and “burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them.”
The Chaldeans, the Ethiopians too, “fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword.”

His children were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house, “and, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house”: a tornado. “It fell upon the young men, and they are dead.” All his children died. How many could deal with that?

Brothers, as a godly man dealing with God and being righteous, the hedge does not just go around you; it goes around your whole house. It protects even your kids. But once you start being evil, or choose to go into Christianity or whatever, God removes that hedge. That is why you hear about sisters getting caught up in dumb stupid stuff: their father is not right.

Job “rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped, And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.”

If all these bad things happened to you, would you still bless the Lord and give him glory, understanding that the Lord allowed Satan to do them? Job could have said, Lord, why did you allow Satan to do this to me? You killed my kids. Some, when bad things happen, say, why is this happening? I’m keeping the commandments. But Job dropped down and praised him: I came into this world with nothing and I am going to leave with nothing. Job is a template of what is going to happen to every last one of us.

Again the sons of God came before the Lord, and Satan came also, “from going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” One of these days we will go over the different things Job went through when Satan attacked: losing money, losing kids. And there are at least five classes put together on how to fight Satan, and the last one is going to be on another level.

“And still he holdeth fast his integrity”: Job never lost his integrity. “Although thou movedst me against him”: Satan moved the Lord against him. That is what Satan means: adversary, accuser.

“Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.” All Job’s riches were taken away, but Job was still good.

“Touch his bone and his flesh”: that is not just his body. It is also his wife, because she is bone of his bone and flesh of his flesh; woman came from man. Satan was about to touch Job’s wife too.

“Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.” Do what you have to do to him, but do not kill him. So you could get sick; all types of things could happen to you, and that is Satan. But who allows him to do it? God.
Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and he sat down among the ashes scraping himself with a potsherd.

“Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Who was speaking? That was Satan. Satan was able to enter into Job’s wife. All the things Job went through were affecting her too: she lost everything, and now she was watching her husband sick, sores all over him. She was under heavy attack, and Satan wore her down and entered into her.

Sisters have to be mindful: do not allow Satan to get up in your head, and do not allow Satan to use you to oppress your husband. A lot of sisters do that, talking to Satan with Satan up in their head. You have to be able to spot Satan, to know when his thoughts are in your mind.

Everything Job went through that we see was physical: he lost his money, everything he had, then got real sick, then his wife told him to curse God and die. But there is a war that takes place internally that nobody sees but you: the war within. Satan was attacking Job’s mind too.

“These three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.” That was Job’s flaw. He was overrighteous.

Elihu’s wrath was kindled “because he justified himself rather than God.” Job said: I am righteous, this is not supposed to happen to me. I made a covenant, I do not look at other women. I am not weak like Adam, hiding sin in my bosom; when my wife came at me, I checked her.

Righteous in his own eyes, he did not see that there was a reason God was doing this, that God was trying to make him better. In his mind he was righteous: I am not like this person, I am not like that person. That was his mistake, and the Lord did not like it.

precepts.why: “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.” Job said he hates himself and repents. Repents for what? For justifying himself and not God, for being righteous in his own eyes. Job repented for what he did.

“Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise.” Don’t be that person who tries to act overrighteous and just ends up looking fake. Over wise is: nobody can say anything to me, I am better than everybody, I know everything. Nobody knows everything. Nobody is perfect. Everyone has some things they are dealing with that they need help with.

Job was overrighteous, and the Lord showed him that. That is why, when Satan attacks, it shows you things inside yourself. With all that Job went through, he became perfect. “Why shouldest thou destroy thyself?” When you are righteous over much, you are destroying yourself.

“In the day of prosperity be joyful”: Job had all those riches, and in that time be joyful. “But in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other.” This is what Job did not understand. You are going through prosperity, but God says, I am about to bring you adversity.

Where does adversity come from? From your adversary: Satan and his children. And things are going to get bad. God set up the adversity; he allowed it to happen to you. Why? “To the end that man should find nothing after him.” God wants you to trust in him. That is why he takes away the prosperity and gives you adversity.

sense.text: “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” Those who are in this truth and have repented: this walk is continual. Satan does not just leave; he will always come back. There is no break in this war, no lunch break, no taking a break from warring with Satan. If you think you stand, beware, because you could fall. Any one of us could fall.

“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.” The things we go through are things everybody goes through: everybody faces death; losing a job, losing a house, having nothing to eat, being put in prison.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able.” God has a say in how Satan deals with you, the same thing we read with Job: do not take his life, but take everything he has and make him sick. Some temptation might be death, might be prison, might be your wife leaving, your children leaving, your children dying in a car accident; the Lord knows he or she can deal with it.

“But will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” The way to escape is to trust in him, trust in his word, worship him. It is going to be hard, but the Lord will give you a way to escape and make sure you are able to bear it.
“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” Temptations are tribulations: Satan attacking you.

“Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.” Being tempted by Satan is to try your faith. Does this brother really believe? Let me allow Satan to jump on his wife and see if he believes. That is how it works. The only way your faith is going to be tried is in temptation. Satan has a job to do: Satan has to tempt you.

“But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire.” When temptation comes, it makes you perfect. Without Satan and without temptation, the saints cannot become perfect; everything works hand in hand. If Satan does not come and tempt you, you cannot become stronger. It is like a soldier fighting an adversary: when you keep fighting, you become experienced in war.

“Wanting nothing”: lacking nothing. The Lord wants us to have strong faith, charity, all these things, so he is going to put us through things. We have to fight through them, and the trials and tribulations that come our way make us better and stronger.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil”: the devil is the deceiver. “As a roaring lion”, “seeking whom he may devour.” That is Satan’s job: to devour you, to destroy you. He walks up and down on the earth, as he said in Job. Once you repent and come to this truth, it is Satan’s job to destroy every last one of us, and he attacks you with your lust and desires.

To be vigilant means you are watching. You have to see Satan before he attacks you; and sometimes you might not see him, but while he is attacking you have to see what it is. Don’t wait until he puts thoughts in your mind and you act on them, and afterwards you are like Judas: what did I do? See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say: get out of my mind, Satan.

“Whom resist stedfast in the faith”: you have to resist Satan. “Knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world”: the same things you are going through, your other brothers are going through. Those afflictions come from your adversary, the devil.

“But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect.” This is the devil’s job: all the temptations and afflictions Satan brings against us are to make us perfect. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

That is a hard saying: without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job, him and his children, to try us. Nobody wants to suffer. But the Lord says, you all want the kingdom, you have to suffer. And if you are acceptable, after you suffer a while you are going to get that kingdom of eternal glory.

Suffering makes you perfect, “stablish”: it establishes you; “strengthen”: when you go through hard things you become battle hardened, like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years; you can’t fight them any old how. “Settle you”: you are settled within your spirit. It is what it is.

precepts.why:
This shows how Satan makes us perfect. “All things are double one against another”: God created good, and he created evil also. “And he hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing.

“One thing establisheth the good of another.” What establishes our good and makes us perfect? Temptation: when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Some brothers and sisters do get devoured. But those who are not devoured become better and become perfect. Learn how to fight him and to see him when he is coming. Don’t wait until he comes on you and then you have to deal with regrets.

“And who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord’s glory.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” The fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through the fire, it does not destroy him; it purifies him and makes him better. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it destroys, and some it makes perfect in the sight of God.

When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some will be destroyed. Some sisters will be up out of here: I ain’t messing with IUIC, the government says they are a hate group. Some brothers will be gone too. But some will be purified and become that pure gold. You have to go through adversity; your enemy has to attack you. That is how you become a better fighter.

sense.text:
“Be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” The wiles of the devil are his tricks. The devil does not attack the same way. The more you grow in this truth and the more you are able to see him, the more he comes different ways, where you cannot see him. He is not going to offer you shrimp fried rice any more; he is coming slick.

The wiles go back to how he tricked Eve: you will not surely die; you will know good and evil like me. Now it could be that sister next to you whispering something in your ear, that brother next to you whispering evil in your ear. Or somebody wrongs you, says I’m sorry, and you take the apology, but in your mind you say, I will never forgive him. That is Satan coming another way.

“For we wrestle not against flesh and blood”: it is not the physical person in front of you that you are fighting. “Against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world”: that is governments. In these governments and high places there are demons working with them, and Satan is working with them.

Who are the rulers of the darkness of this world today? Esau, Satan’s children, the so-called white men, the Caucasian race. They are the fourth beast, the false prophets and the rulers of darkness of this world. “Against spiritual wickedness in high places”: governments.

“That ye may be able to withstand in the evil day.” Remember Job’s evil day: in one day he lost all his riches, and then he got sick. We all have that evil day coming, when the Lord says, this day I am going to try you. You have been in this truth three years, four years; let me see if you endure and stay, or leave.

“And having done all, to stand.” Sometimes things are out of your hands and there is nothing you can do, but you still have to stand, because you could fall. In fighting Satan some of us will fall. Some fell this week, caught up in fornication; some are still in the midst of fornication, adultery, all forms of wickedness. Satan is whooping your ass; you are on the floor and he is stomping your behind out.

If you need help, ask us to pray for you. Some are dealing with demons, and the only way those demons leave is by fasting and prayer.
“Having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace”: you still go and teach. You are out there teaching.

“Above all, taking the shield of faith”: your shield is faith, “wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.” The wicked are Satan and his children, the rulers of the darkness of this world. All these pieces of armour are to be broken down another day; the Bishop went over this years ago, and it is good to revisit.
“And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.” The word of God is your weapon that you are using to fight.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” Where do the evil thoughts come from? Your mind. In fighting Satan, where does the fight start first and foremost? It always starts with your mind. A lot of brothers and sisters fall in this truth because they do not know that; they wait until after their mind is defiled.

“Adulteries, fornications, murders”: how does that get in your mind? What is it doing there?
“Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye”: envy; “blasphemy, pride, foolishness.”

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” That is the war you are fighting within you. How do those evil things get into your mind and defile you? Remember who you are warring against: Satan. We have to fight first in our mind.

precepts.why:
This shows how the evil things get in your mind. Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession and kept back part of the price. “But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost”? That lying spirit comes from Satan. Satan filled his heart to lie.

So when it says out of the heart of men proceed evil thoughts, what does Satan do? He whispers thoughts in your mind. He is there in your head, tempting you, putting things there that are not there. The Deacon says something to you, and Satan says: why did he say that to you? Deacon don’t like you. Satan puts things in everyone’s head, all of us. The war always starts in the mind.

To win the fight, you have to learn to kill him there. When Satan puts thoughts in your mind, they should never become action. Don’t act on it. Ask yourself, why am I thinking like this? Why are these thoughts in my mind? Then go and fast and pray: Lord, take these thoughts out of my mind.

A husband tells his wife, make sure you clean up the bathroom, it hasn’t been cleaned in two days. Men give orders, men don’t ask; a man of God is going to order his wife, command his wife. Real men do not talk soft: hey baby, how you doing. Sisters, any brother talking like that to you, dump him, and let us know who he is, so all the sisters know that brother is weak; we are going to make a list of brothers for sisters not to marry. Some brothers, I see the softness in you, but we are going to build you up. Men of God don’t beg: baby, can you please clean the house; baby, can you please give me some tonight, I’m horny. No. Weak brothers don’t want to become like Christ, like Adam and rule, like Abraham and command his house.

Then the voice comes, and it is Satan filling the heart: you going to let him talk to you like that? Does he not see you homeschooling the kids, making him breakfast, going to school, handling everything else in the house? That is Satan, sisters. A lot of you be saying that crap: you don’t know how much I be doing; I homeschool the kids, I clean, I cook, and then when you come home at nine, ten o’clock I’m tired and you want sex; I got to do all of that. He don’t understand you, he don’t love you: that is Satan whispering in your ears. It happens to every last one of you. Say: that is Satan; why am I thinking like this? The evil thoughts in your mind are an attack. See him when he is coming. That is where the war starts: in your mind.

The sister answers that voice with the word: a soft answer turns away wrath, but harsh words “stir up anger.” That is the fight right there. That is the war. What is she using? The word of God, and that is what we all have to use.

Satan will come at you and say: this brother don’t like you; why did he do this; why did he say it that way? It is not just sisters with their husbands; it happens with all of us. A lot of the time we deal with the fight externally, when people attack you. But Satan comes in your mind with evil thoughts, bitterness, a root of bitterness, trying to defile you. She could become bitter toward her husband: he’s abusive, he keeps commanding me. Brothers become bitter too. If she listens to Satan, it is going to show in her actions: she becomes disrespectful. But the word of God is in her, and she is acting right.

Respond, don’t react; strength is self-control. Who will you choose, what will you do: flesh over spirit? It is up to you. Crashing out will get you cast out, cast out of my house. Offence, when you hold on to it, turns into grudges, and Satan’s job is to defile your mind. So guard your mind and shake off the thoughts that come. Satan is not only coming physically, like the Chaldeans, or the big booty woman on your job. The demon himself literally comes and whispers things in your ears.
